about: Skills tool: units and significant figures (math chapter, then Units 3, 6 and 8). Each item is generated by ApChemMath.units.generate and graded by ApChemQuestions on value, units and significant figures separately. The validator regenerates 300 items per context, recomputes each answer and runs the grader on the key and on every authored mistake. Explore (tools v2, docs/tools-v2-units-sig-figs-brief.md) is data too: explore.convert (a flask of water and four conversion factors that cancel units in a chain) and explore.read (a graduated cylinder and a beaker read to one estimated digit); the validator recomputes both.
intro: The calculation habits that cost points on every exam. Explore shows the two ideas underneath them: a conversion factor is a fraction worth 1, so a unit on top cancels the same unit on the bottom; and an instrument’s marks decide how many digits of a measurement are real (the digits you read from the marks, plus one you estimate). Test yourself grades each answer three ways, on the value, the unit and the significant figures, with a note on any slip.
howItWorks:
• Multiply or divide: keep the fewest significant figures in the data.
  • Add or subtract: keep the fewest decimal places.
  • Logarithms (pH): the decimal places equal the significant figures of the concentration.
  • Temperature: gas laws and thermodynamics need kelvin, K = °C + 273.15.
  • R: 0.08206 L·atm/(mol·K) with atm and L; 8.314 J/(mol·K) with joules (and kPa·L); 62.36 L·torr/(mol·K) with torr.
  • Energy: report the unit asked for (kJ/mol, not J/mol), with the sign of the process.

Type the number and its unit in their own boxes. Powers of ten can be typed as 1.8e-5 or 1.8 × 10^-5.
